Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

could you put together a practical family trip plan for san diego? we are five people: me and my husband, our kids who are 8 and 13, and my mother, who is 68. we are looking at september 19 through september 25, 2026, so six nights, but we have not booked anything yet. those dates are the school break we can use, not a promise that every activity will be open or that we can get a room. we would fly from denver. please help us think through a realistic trip rather than making it sound like we can do every attraction in town.

we have not bought flights, and we haven't decided whether to rent a car. my mother can walk comfortably for about 20 minutes at a time, but hills and long stretches standing are hard on her knee. she can use ordinary stairs slowly and does not use a wheelchair. please don't assume she can keep up with a full day on foot. the kids are fine walking more, so the plan needs to avoid making her the reason everyone misses things while also giving her real rest time. we could split up for a couple of hours if that makes sense, though we'd rather do most things together. the 8-year-old gets carsick on winding roads, which is part of why i'm unsure about a car.

for lodging, we'd like one room or suite for all five if that's realistic, with two beds plus a sofa bed or similar; a kitchenette would be useful but is not essential. our comfortable target is around $350 per night before taxes, and we'd stretch to $425 if the location saves a lot of driving or makes the days easier. that is a lodging target, not a whole-trip budget. we'd prefer a place with breakfast nearby or included and a pool, but those are preferences, not deal breakers. please compare a couple of suitable areas, not a long directory of hotels. we haven't picked up a rental-car reservation or bought attraction tickets either.

things we'd like to consider are the zoo, one beach visit, the USS Midway, and either Balboa Park museums or a similar cultural stop. the zoo is the one thing all five of us are especially interested in; the kids also want time at the beach and my mother likes gardens and local history. the younger one asked, “can we do one thing where we don't have to stand in a line?” so some easy outdoor time would help. nobody wants a packed schedule. we don't know whether the zoo and Balboa Park should be on the same day, and i don't know how tiring either option is. please give us a sensible order and say where you would leave open time, rather than treating every item as mandatory.

food is fairly simple but needs thought. my mother avoids very spicy food, and the 8-year-old has a mild peanut allergy. it has never caused a reaction that needed emergency treatment, but we check labels and ask restaurants about cross-contact. please include practical meal ideas and don't treat a restaurant as safe without confirming its current allergy practices. we are happy with casual places, grocery-store breakfasts, and bringing snacks. one child is picky about sauces but will eat plain noodles, rice, chicken, fruit, and cheese. we don't need reservations made; suggestions for when reservations may be useful are enough.

1. the trip should include a realistic arrival day and departure day, not a full sightseeing day on each end. our flight times aren't known. please show how the outline changes if we land late or have an early flight home.
2. include a rough daily rhythm with one main activity at most, meal breaks, and downtime. my mother usually rests after lunch for at least an hour, and the younger child gets grumpy if lunch is pushed much past 12:30.
3. explain the practical transport tradeoffs between staying without a car and renting one for some or all of the trip. we'd like to know whether the places we named can work together without exhausting everyone. don't assume that using a rideshare is easy for five people with bags.
4. give a rough cost picture for lodging, local transport or car, admissions, and food, but label estimates as estimates and don't include airfare as if you know its price. we can spend more on one special day, but we are trying to avoid surprise costs.

we'd rather have a plan with a couple of alternatives than a confident answer based on details we haven't settled. flag anything that depends on opening days, ticket availability, actual flight times, or the exact hotel location. if you need to suggest we drop one of the attractions, explain why and offer a calmer replacement. don't make the entire week about the zoo, even though it is the top priority. the overall goal is a trip that feels like a holiday for the adults as well as something fun for the kids, and that my mother can enjoy without having to push through knee pain.", "output": "Create a practical, realistic six-night family trip plan for San Diego for September 19–25, 2026. We are five travelers: two adults, children ages 8 and 13, and my 68-year-old mother. We would fly from Denver. We have not booked flights, lodging, a rental car, or attraction tickets, and the dates reflect our available school break rather than confirmed bookings. Do not assume activities will be open or rooms available; flag details that depend on opening days, ticket availability, flight times, or the exact hotel location.

**Travelers and pace**
My mother can walk comfortably for about 20 minutes at a time, but hills and long periods of standing are difficult because of her knee. She can manage ordinary stairs slowly and does not use a wheelchair. Build in a rest after lunch of at least an hour, and do not plan a full day on foot. The children can walk farther. We would prefer to do most activities together, but could split up for a couple of hours if that would help. The 8-year-old gets carsick on winding roads, so take that into account when considering a rental car. The younger child also gets grumpy if lunch is much later than 12:30.

**Lodging and transport**
Compare a couple of suitable areas, not a long list of hotels. We would like one room or suite for all five, ideally with two beds and a sofa bed or similar. A kitchenette would be useful but is not essential. Our comfortable lodging target is about $350 per night before taxes; we could stretch to $425 if the location substantially reduces driving or makes the days easier. This is a lodging target, not a total-trip budget. Breakfast nearby or included and a pool are preferences, not requirements.

Explain the practical tradeoffs between staying without a car and renting one for some or all of the trip. Consider whether the zoo, beach, USS Midway, and a cultural stop can fit together without exhausting the group. Do not assume rideshares are easy for five people with bags, and do not assume we have already reserved a car.

**Activities and meals**
We would like to consider the zoo, one beach visit, the USS Midway, and either Balboa Park museums or a similar cultural stop. The zoo is the one activity all five are especially interested in. The children also want beach time, and my mother enjoys gardens and local history. The 8-year-old asked, “can we do one thing where we don't have to stand in a line?” Include some easy outdoor time. We are unsure whether the zoo and Balboa Park belong on the same day and how tiring either would be. Recommend a sensible order, leave open time, and do not treat every activity as mandatory. If you recommend dropping an attraction, explain why and suggest a calmer replacement. Do not make the whole week about the zoo.

My mother avoids very spicy food. The 8-year-old has a mild peanut allergy; it has not caused a reaction requiring emergency treatment, but we check labels and ask about cross-contact. Include practical meal ideas, but do not describe any restaurant as safe without confirming its current allergy practices. Casual restaurants, grocery-store breakfasts, and snacks are welcome. The picky eater will eat plain noodles, rice, chicken, fruit, and cheese, but is particular about sauces. We do not need reservations made; just note when reservations may be useful.

**Please include:**
1. A realistic arrival day and departure day, without assuming either is a full sightseeing day. Flight times are unknown; show how the outline could change with a late arrival or early return flight.
2. A rough daily rhythm with no more than one main activity per day, meal breaks, and downtime. Keep lunch by 12:30 and include at least an hour of rest after lunch for my mother.
3. A rough cost picture for lodging, local transport or a car, admissions, and food. Label costs as estimates, exclude airfare rather than guessing its price, and note ways to avoid surprise costs. We can spend more on one special day but want to manage the rest of the budget.

Offer a couple of alternatives rather than relying on details we have not settled. The goal is a holiday that is enjoyable for the adults as well as the children, and that my mother can take part in without pushing through knee pain."}]
